maḫrum: front, before (Harper’s maḫru): ina maḫra (maḫ-ra) “in front”, of fates that go before a god; the exact force UNCERTAIN
abkallum: wise one, leader (Harper’s abkallu, written NUN.ME): abkal ilī “leader of the gods” (abkal the form before a genitive; ilī written NI.NI)
arākum-Š: Š-stem of arākum “to be long”: to lengthen, make long · mušarriku (mu-ša-ri-ku, Š participle, Harper’s arāku III,1) “who lengthens”; the final -u is a nominative vowel kept in the construct
mišītum: oblivion, forgetting (Harper’s mišîtu): mišītim (mi-ši-tim, genitive after ina) “in oblivion”
nārum: river (written ÍD; the doubled sign ÍD.ÍD marks the plural): nārātum “rivers” · nārātīšu (ÍD.ÍD-šu) “his rivers”
sekērum: to shut off, block (Harper’s sakâru, glossed by him “to dam up”): liskir (li-is-ki-ir, precative) “let him block”
Ašnan: Ašnan ({d}ŠE.TIR, the star + ŠE + TIR) — the grain-deity (a goddess in modern accounts); the word is also grain itself: napišti nišī “the life of the people”
ešērum-Št: Št-stem of ešērum “to be straight”: to guide aright · muštēšir (mu-uš-te-še-ir, Št participle) “who guides”; the same verb as šutēšurum in the litany
tukultum: trust, support (Harper’s tukultu, glossed by him “strength”): tukultī (tu-kul-ti, the suffix -ī “my” not written out) “my trust”, UNCERTAIN; the GUL sign is read kul
sakāpum: to overthrow (Harper’s sakâpu): liskip (li-is-ki-ip, precative) “let him overthrow”
ešûm: to confuse, cause to err (Harper’s ešû I,1; a base sense “to be confused, go astray” is inferred): liši (li-ši) “let him confuse”, UNCERTAIN in form and sense
ummānum: army, host: ummānišu (um-ma-ni-šu) “his army”; išid ummānišu “the foundation of his army”
ḫalāṣum-Š: Š-stem of ḫalāṣum: to destroy (Harper’s ḫalṣû III,1) · lišḫelṣi (li-iš-ḫi-[el]-ṣi, Š precative) “let him destroy”, UNCERTAIN; the sign el is partly dotted on the plate, so Harper brackets [el]; the sign ZI is read ṣi
bīrum: sight, vision (Harper’s bīru): bīrišu (bi-ri-šu) “his sight”; ina bīrišu “in his sight”
lemnum: evil, bad: lemnam (lim-nam, accusative) “an evil omen”
marūštum: grievous, blighting (Harper’s marūštu): marūštum (ma-ru-uš-tum, feminine nominative) “grievous”, of a word (awātum)
arḫiš: quickly, speedily (adverb in -iš, Harper’s arḫiš): ar-ḫi-iš
balṭum: alive, living (Harper’s baltu): balṭūtim (ba-al-tu-tim, genitive plural, TU written for ṭu) “among the living”; ina balṭūtim
ekimmum: spirit of the dead, ghost (Harper’s ekimmu, written GEKIM; modern GIDIM): the doubled sign GIDIM.GIDIM marks the plural, ekimmêšu (GIDIM.GIDIM-šu) “his spirits”; the sign identification is TENTATIVE
zamûm-Š: Š-stem of zamûm (Harper’s zamû III,1 “to deprive”; his glossary has no simple stem, so “to lack, be deprived” is inferred and UNCERTAIN): to deprive, taking two accusatives · lišazmi (li-ša-az-mi, Š precative) “let him deprive”: mê lišazmi “let him deprive (them) of water”
šērtum: sword, scimitar (Harper’s šêrtu, the second of his two nouns of this spelling, glossed “sword, scimitar”; the sense UNCERTAIN): šērissu (še-ri-zu, with -šu, the t and š said ss, written ZU) “his sword”; perhaps a weapon of the moon-god · a different word from šērtum-sin
šērtum-sin: sin, guilt (Harper’s šêrtu “sin”, the first of his two nouns of this spelling): šērissu (še-ri-zu, with -šu) “his sin”, šērissu rabītam “his great sin” · a different word from šērtum “sword”
zumrum: body: zumrišu (zu-um-ri-šu) “his body”; ina zumrišu “in his body”
dimmatum: tears, weeping, lament: dimmatim (di-im-ma-tim, genitive) “of weeping”; ina tanēḫim u dimmatim “in sighing and weeping”
qatûm-Š: Š-stem of qatûm “to come to an end” (Harper’s qatû III,1): to bring to an end, cut off · lišaqti (li-ša-aq-ti, Š precative; AK read aq) “let him bring to an end”
kammalum: burden, ignominy (Harper’s kammalu): kammal (kam-ma-al, the form before a genitive) “the burden of”: kammal šarrūtim “the burden of kingship”
gugallum: regent (Harper’s gugallu, syllabic gu-gal), the title of the god who oversees the canals; modern editions take it as “canal-inspector”: gugal šamê u erṣetim “the regent of heaven and earth”
zunnum: rain (Harper’s zunnu): zunnī (zu-ni) “rains”, a plural form
mīlum: flood, high water (Harper’s “water-flood”): mīlam (mi-lam, accusative) “the flood”
bubūtum: hunger (Harper’s bûbûtu): bubūtim (bu-bu-tim, genitive) “of hunger”; ina ḫušaḫḫim u bubūtim “with famine and hunger”
nisûm: to break loose, storm (Harper’s nisû I,1) · lissima (li-is-si-ma, li- + the verb + -ma “and”) “let him storm, and”; the verb is UNCERTAIN
tīlum: mound, heap of ruins (Harper’s telu “hill, heap”): til (written with the BAD sign) in tīl abūbim “a mound of the flood”
abūbum: the flood, the Deluge (Harper’s ABUBU, glossed by him “hurricane”; the flood is the modern sense): abūbim (a-bu-bi-im, genitive) “of the flood”

__broaden__.agûm: crown · written with one logogram AGA₃ (the sign of AGA₃.ÚS in laws-26-41) at XLIII 45, agâm (accusative) “the crown”, the sign TENTATIVE; the litany spells it syllabically a-gi-im
__broaden__.balāṭum: to live; D-stem bulluṭum — muballiṭ “who gives life” · stative baltat (ba-al-ṭa-at) “she lives”, in adi baltat “as long as she lives” · the noun “life”: balāṭam (ba-la-ṭam, accusative) “a life”; balāṭīya (ba-la-ṭi-ia) “my life”; ūm balāṭīya “the days of my life”
__broaden__.šadālum: to be wide; D-stem — mušaddil “who widens” · lišaddilšu (li-ša-ad-di-il-šu, precative + -šu, Harper’s šadālu II,1, D-stem, glossed by him “to extend, to multiply”) “let him increase (for him)”: kammal šarrūtim lišaddilšu “let him increase for him the burden of kingship”, UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.uznum: ear: uznašu (written u-zu-un-šu, with no vowel between un and šu; Harper normalizes accusative + -šu) “his ear”; the noun has no plural ending here, so one ear · noun · uznam (uz-na-am, accusative) “ear”, and by extension “understanding”: uznam u nēmeqam “understanding and wisdom”
__broaden__.warḫum: month (written with ITI, the moon-month sign): warḫim “of the month” · warḫušu (ITI-šu) “his month”, nominative with -šu (Harper normalizes arḫišu) · arḫī (the sign ITI written twice, ITI.ITI; the doubled sign marks the plural) “months”: ūmī arḫī šanāt palêšu “the days, months, years of his reign”
__broaden__.ūmum: day; ūmišu “daily” (written UD-mi-šu) · plural “days”: ūmī (written UD-mi-) “days”: ina ūmīšu lā malûtim “in his days not full” (the days of a lease) · ūm “day” (UD), before a following word, in ūm NER lā “a day (when ?) NER not …” · ūmīšu (UD-mi-šu) “his days”: ūmīšu imannûma “they shall count his days” · ina ūmim (i-na UD) “per day, by the day”, with the numeral 1{kam}: ina ūmim 1{kam} 180 qa “for each day 180 qa”; the day-rate formula of §271–277 · ūmī (the sign UD alone) “days”: ūmī iṣūtim “few days” · ūmī (UD-mi) “days” in a list with arḫī “months” and šanāt “years”; ūm (UD-um) “day(s) of” before a genitive: ūm balāṭīya “the days of my life”
__broaden__.šattum: year: šattam (syllabic, §31) or MU (the year-sign, §30) · šattim (genitive); plural šanātim “years” (ša šanātim “of the years”); MU 4{kam}, said erbe šanātim “four years” · MU 3{kam}, said šalāš šanātim “for three years”; šanat (ša-na-at) “(in) the year”, ina šanat “each year” · šanāt (ša-na-a-at) “the years of”, the plural construct before a genitive: šanāt palêšu “the years of his reign”
__broaden__.alākum: to go: illak “he shall go” · illiku “(where) he went” (preterite, subjunctive -u, after a restored ašar), in the agent law · alākišu (a-la-ki-šu) “his going” (infinitive with -šu): ina alākišu “in his going” · Gt present ittallak (it-ta-al-la-ak) “she shall go away” (the Gt gives the sense of going off; the Gtn would be ittanallak) · ittalak “she has gone” (perfect): ana šīmtim ittalak “she has gone to her fate” · ittalku (it-ta-al-ku) with the subjunctive -u: warka abum ana šīmtim ittalku “after the father has gone to his fate” · ittalkamma (it-ta-al-kam-ma) perfect ittalkam (ittalak + the ventive -am, “hither”) “he has come”, + -ma “and” · lillikma (li-il-li-ik-ma, li- + illik + -ma) “let him go, and” · illakā (i-la-ka) “they go”, present 3rd feminine plural, agreeing with a feminine plural noun: ša šīmātūšu ina maḫra illakā “whose fates go in front”
__broaden__.-ia: my · written -ia after a consonant or Sumerogram (URU-ia, ALAN-ia, utlīya, narûya); the plural nouns take -ūa or -īya (awâtūa, uṣurātūa, uṣurātīya); bare -ī in ṣillī, šumī · on a singular nominative: rēṣūa (ri-zu-u-a, ZU read ṣu) “my helper”
__broaden__.-ī: my (1st-person possessive suffix) · on a participle: bānî (ba-ni-i, banûm “to create” + -ī) “my creator”
__broaden__.târum-D: D-stem of târum: to give back: turru “taken away/captured”; utarrūšumma “they shall return (it) to him” · utâr (present) “he shall hand back” · turrim (infinitive, tu-ur-ri-im): ana turrim “for repaying, to give back”; utâr (present) “he shall hand back” · uttēr (ut-te-ir, perfect) “he has given back”: the same verb as utâr · litēršu (li-te-ir-šu, precative + -šu, Harper’s taru II,1) “let him turn back / take back from him”, UNCERTAIN: melam šarrūtim litēršu “let him turn the glory of kingship away from him” · litēr (li-te-ir, precative, without a suffix) “let him turn”: ana tīl abūbim litēr “let him turn (it) into a mound of the flood”
__broaden__.târum: to return: ul itârma “he shall never again …” · itâr (i-ta-ar) “he shall go back”: ana bīt abišu itâr “he shall go back to his father’s house” · littarrūšu (li-it-ta-ar-ru-šu, li- + a t-stem form + -šu, Harper’s târu I,2, the Gt) “let him bring him”, UNCERTAIN in form (the ending -ū looks plural, “let them”?) and in sense: mišītim littarrūšu “bring him to oblivion”
__broaden__.bašûm-Š: Š-stem of bašûm “to exist”: to bring into being, produce (a crop): uštabši “he has produced” (perfect) · uštabši (uš-tab-ši) “he has brought about” (perfect): kazzatam uštabši “he has brought about a harm (?)” · ušabšû (u-ša-ab-šu-u) “which he brought about” (preterite + relative -u) · šubšâm (šu-ub-ša-a-am, Š infinitive, accusative) “to bring into being”: lā šubšâm “not to bring into being”, Harper’s basu III,1 (su-ub-sa-a-am), with no sense given by him · ušabši (u-ša-ab-ši, preterite 3rd singular, after ay) “(may he not) bring into being”: ay ušabši
__broaden__.šakānum: to set, place: išakkanūšumma “they shall set for him (a term), and” · išakkanūšum (present, plural, dative -šum) “they shall place (it) for him”, i.e. count it to him · iššakkan (iš-ša-ak-ka-an, N-stem present) “it shall be put”: ul iššakkan “it shall not be put (in the account)” · to set, put, impose: ištakan (iš-ta-ka-an, perfect, “has set”), išakkan (present) — išakkanšima (i-ša-ak-ka-an-ši-ma, with -ši and -ma) “he/she shall set (it) on her, and”, as in abbuttam išakkan · išakkanūši “they shall set (her on a stake)”, išakkanūšumma “they shall set (it) aside for him, and” · idiom panam šakānum (panam ištakan) “to set the face” = to make up one’s mind · iššakkan also written iš-ta-ak-ka-an (Harper’s reading, UNCERTAIN): andurār amtim iššakkan “the release of the slave-woman shall be established” · iššakkan (iš-ša-ak-ka-an, N-stem present) “it shall be set”: andurāršunu iššakkan “their release shall be set” · šaknāt (ša-ak-na-at, feminine plural stative) “those set (with)”: šaknāt napištim “those set with life”, i.e. those who have life, UNCERTAIN · liškunšum (li-iš-ku-un-šum, G precative + -šum) “let him set for him”
__broaden__.bēlum: owner, lord: bēl ḫulqim “owner of the lost property” · owner of a field, bēl eqlim; bēl ḫubullim “creditor” · bēl kirîm “owner of the orchard” · bēl (be-el), the construct “owner of”, also with a suffix on the noun that follows: bēl ḫubullišu “his creditor”, bēl ḫubulliša “her creditor” · bēl (be-el, not the sign EN) “owner of”: bēl aššatim “the owner of the wife”, i.e. the man entitled to her (my reading) · bēlišu (be-li-šu) “its owner” (of an animal), bēlišuma “to its owner only” (with the emphatic -ma); bēl alpim “the owner of the ox” · bēl epinnim “the owner of the plough”, bēl tarbaṣim “the owner of the pen”; bēlīšunu (be-li-šu-nu) “their owners”, the owners of the cattle and sheep a herdsman has lost · bēl (be-el) “owner of” before a genitive: bēl wardim “the owner of the male slave” · bēlī (be-li) “my master”: ul bēlī atta “you are not my master” · bēlšu, bēlišu (be-el-šu, be-li-šu) “his master” · bēlum (be-lum, the full nominative, not the construct bēl) “the lord”, standing alone as a title after epithets: bēlum tukultī “the lord, my trust”, UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.šīrum: flesh, body; wellbeing · šīr (SU, bound form before a genitive) “flesh of”: šīr pasuttišu “the flesh of its pasuttu” · šīram (written UZU, Harper’s List no. 80; the sign TENTATIVE) “omen, oracle” (Harper’s ŠÎRU “oracle”): šīram lemnam “an evil omen”
__broaden__.nasāḫum: to pull out, uproot; of a son, to cast out, disinherit (Harper: “to cut off, to disinherit”): nasāḫim (na-sa-ḫi-im, infinitive) “to cast out”; anassaḫ (a-na-za-aḫ) “I shall cast out” (first person present); inassaḫ (i-na-za-aḫ) “he shall cast out” (third person present) · inassaḫū (i-na-za-ḫu) “they shall pluck out”, present plural: īnšu inassaḫū “they shall pluck out his eye” (the ZA sign for sa) · nasāḫim (na-sa-ḫi-im) infinitive “to cast out”: ana tarbītim nasāḫim “to cast out the foster-child” · assuḫ (az-zu-uḫ, preterite, 1st person) “I tore out”, of enemies · lissuḫ (li-zu-uḫ, precative, the n assimilated and the ss written with ZU) “let him uproot”: raggam u ṣēnam lissuḫ “let him uproot the wicked and the evil one” · nasāḫ (na-sa-aḫ, infinitive in the construct) “the uprooting of”: nasāḫ išid šarrūtišu “the uprooting of the foundation of his kingship” · lissuḫšu (li-iz-zu-uḫ-šu, precative + -šu, the n assimilated, ZU for ss) “let him uproot him”
__broaden__.ḫalāqum: to be lost, vanish: ḫalqu, ḫalqam · iḫtaliq (iḫ-ta-li-iq, perfect) “it has been lost”; ḫaliq (ḫa-li-iq, stative) “(it) is lost”, ḫaliqma “is lost, and”; lā ḫaliqma “is not lost, and” · ḫalāq (ḫa-la-aq, infinitive in the construct) “the loss of”: ḫalāq mātišu “the loss of his land” · iḫalliqu (i-ḫal-li-qu₂, present with the subjunctive -u) “(which) will vanish”: ša ina zumrišu lā iḫalliqu “which will not vanish in his body”
__broaden__.kašādum: to reach, overcome: iktašassu “(the River) has overcome him” · likšussu (li-ik-šu-zu, precative + -šu, the d and š said ss, written ZU) “let it reach him, overtake him”
__broaden__.šūpûm: to make appear, make manifest (š-stem of wapûm) · šūpât (šu-pa-a-at, stative) “it shines forth, is made to appear” (Harper: “to shine”)
__broaden__.emēdum: to lay on, impose; with arnam, arnam emēdum “to lay guilt (on oneself)”, i.e. to be in the wrong (Harper emēdu I,1): immidū (i-im-mi-du) “they have laid (guilt), they are in the wrong” (preterite, 3rd plural; the -u is the plural ending, the doubled m is the assimilated d of the root, spelled out in the sign mi); the whole sense of the clause, “the sons are in the wrong”, rests on this reading and is UNCERTAIN in its grammar · limussuma (li-mu-zu-ma, li- + the verb + -šu + -ma) “let him lay upon him, and” (Harper’s emēdu II,1, a D-stem); the vowel u of the spelling is not explained, so the form is UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.šanānum: to rival (Harper’s šananu): šāninam (ša-ni-nam, accusative) “a rival”; the clause it stands in is UNCERTAIN · šitannu (ši-ta-an-nu, Harper’s šanānu I,2, a t-stem) “(a life which) is the match of (death)”, UNCERTAIN in form: balāṭam ša itti mūtim šitannu
__broaden__.šâmum: to buy: ištām “he bought”, išammu “he buys” · ALSO a second verb of the same spelling, “to fix, decree” (destinies, well-being): išīm (i-ši-im) “he decreed”, išīmam (i-ši-ma-am) “he decreed for me” (preterite + the ventive -am) · lišīmšum (li-ši-im-šum, precative + -šum) “let him decree for him”: ana šīmtim lišīmšum “let him decree for him as fate”
__broaden__.ḫalāqum-D: D-stem of ḫalāqum “to be lost, to perish”: to destroy, cause to be lost: uḫalliqu (preterite, with the relative -u) “(the grain) he destroyed” · uḫtalliq (uḫ-ta-al-li-iq, perfect, 3rd singular) “he has destroyed”: šumma makkūr uḫtalliq “if he has destroyed property”; of a boatman, ù lū uḫtalliq “or has destroyed (it)” · liḫalliq (li-ḫal-li-iq, precative with li-, as litēr; a D precative is normally lu-, so the form is UNCERTAIN) “let him destroy”: mātassu ... liḫalliq “let him destroy his land”
__broaden__.kussûm: chair, seat ({giš}GU.ZA) — the seat of office · kussâm (accusative) “the throne”: agâm kussâm ša šarrūtim “the crown, the throne of kingship”
__broaden__.erṣetum: earth, land, territory: erṣetišunu “their territory” · erṣetim (ir-ṣi-tim, genitive) “of earth”: šamê u erṣetim “of heaven and earth”, ina erṣetim “in the earth” · erṣetīšu (ir-ṣi-ti-šu) “his land”

ezzum: furious, raging (Harper’s ezzu, adverb ezziš “furiously”) · izziš (iz-zi-iš, with i for e, adverb in -iš) “furiously”
